source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
CyrusOne's Allen campus publishes 77 MW of IT capacity, second among Texas data centers that publish power figures, but its compliance certifications and unstated expansion plans leave its AI role unresolved.

Texas maps 133 data center sites and publishes capacity for fewer than one in seven of them. The disclosed state total is 475 MW, so this campus accounts for about a sixth of the capacity Texas actually reports. At 40 kW per rack, 77 MW is roughly 1,900 racks of compute. Dallas-Fort Worth has established power and fiber, but it is not among the largest AI cluster regions published to date.

The certifications are the more telling detail. HIPAA, FISMA, PCI DSS, ISO 27001, and SSAE 16 Type II fit tenants with regulated data, not AI training, which carries no standard compliance requirement. Green Globes rewards efficiency, a secondary concern when power is the binding constraint. The suitability score of 76 is derived from published IT capacity and operator type, and no announced expansion is recorded.

What the data does not cover is whether CyrusOne intends to add capacity at Allen, how the 77 MW is contracted, or what share serves AI workloads. The 976,000 square feet of technical space and the three facility codes describe a colocation campus rather than a purpose-built AI site. Nothing here says the campus cannot host AI, only that its published qualifications point elsewhere.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
